habits.scope_condition: Applies to hotels after evening fairs, receptions, late arrivals, or suburban venue stays where convenient dinner access matters.

habits.boundary_condition: Evidence supports queen-size beds as the recurring preference. A king bed may be acceptable when explicitly offered or requested, but the evidence does not establish a reusable preference to upgrade to king whenever possible.
habits.condition: When booking a standard hotel room where a single larger/shared bed is appropriate and no separate-bed setup has been requested.
habits.default_action: Filter for or request a queen-size bed when bed type is selectable; if the listing only shows double, twin, or unspecified bedding, confirm the bed setup before booking.
habits.exception_condition: Honor explicit requests for twin beds, multiple separate beds, multiple rooms with different bedding, accessibility-related bedding, or any other trip-specific bed arrangement.
habits.name: queen_bed_for_single_bed_hotel_rooms
habits.preference_value: Prefer a queen-size bed for hotel rooms intended to have one larger/shared bed.
habits.scope_condition: Applies to standard hotel rooms for solo work travel or spouse/family weekend stays when a single larger-bed room is the appropriate setup.

longitudinal_plan.travel_tempo: Roughly two academic-year cycles, with dense fall recruitment periods, a smaller spring event wave, a few summer conferences, and scattered personal weekends. Expect about 24 to 30 distinct trip-planning episodes spread across the sessions.

typical_episode_shape.conference_trip: Block hotel comparison, flight timing check, and one follow-up to reconcile reimbursement or agenda constraints.
typical_episode_shape.personal_weekend: Shorter planning thread with flights and a practical hotel, usually reusing comfort defaults without extensive optimization.
typical_episode_shape.work_trip: Initial route and hotel search, refinement around event times, final shortlist or booking summary, and occasional change handling when fair schedules move.

persona.decision_posture: Organized, schedule-aware, and practical. She values predictable flights and easy food logistics more than luxury, and treats most preferences as soft when fair times, campus events, availability, or reimbursement rules dominate.
persona.name: Tessa Alvarez
persona.occupation: regional admissions recruiter for a private university
persona.travel_identity: Seasonal self-booking traveler who plans recruitment loops, admitted-student receptions, higher-ed conferences, and occasional family weekends.

travel_contexts.description: August through November trips to high-school visits, college fairs, and counselor breakfasts across the Mountain West, Pacific Northwest, Texas, and upper Midwest.
travel_contexts.planning_notes: Often multi-city, with morning school appointments and evening fair commitments.

travel_contexts.description: February through April travel for admitted-student receptions, transfer fairs, alumni-hosted meetups, and counselor follow-ups.
travel_contexts.planning_notes: More date-constrained than fall travel, with hotels often near suburban event venues.

travel_contexts.description: A few annual higher-education and admissions conferences, sometimes involving conference hotel blocks and tighter flight windows.
travel_contexts.planning_notes: She compares official blocks against nearby practical alternatives.

travel_contexts.description: Occasional trips with her spouse or one of her teenagers to visit relatives, attend tournaments, or add a short leisure weekend after work travel.
travel_contexts.planning_notes: These are less frequent but reuse many of her comfort defaults.

planning_behaviors: Asks for options to be grouped by practicality, not just lowest price.
Appreciates explicit notes when a hotel is missing an expected room or recovery amenity.
Wants booking caveats stated plainly before she commits.
communication_style.preferred_detail_level: Likes compact shortlists with the deciding trade-offs called out clearly rather than long narrative descriptions.

habit_interactions: Hotel reliability and in-room routine usually matter more than decorative room features, especially before teaching days.
Recovery amenities are most salient on multi-night work trips and active leisure weekends, but she will consider close matches if the schedule or location is better.
Return-flight timing is evaluated around whether she can finish a course, get to the airport without rushing, and still be functional the next day.
Seat preference is independent of carrier choice; she has no stable airline default because Tampa routings vary by destination and price.
She does not show a stable recurring preference for hotel breakfast, restaurant access, or balconies; those arise only when a specific trip calls for them.

habits.boundary_condition: Applies only to seat location. If seat selection is unavailable at booking or is deferred until check-in, note that limitation and try to secure a window seat at the earliest available time.
habits.condition: When booking or selecting seats for flights where a seat location preference can be applied.
habits.default_action: Prefer or request a window seat by default.
habits.exception_condition: Use a different seat only if the user specifies another seat preference, needs a different seating arrangement, or no acceptable window seat is available.
habits.name: prefers_window_seat_on_flights
habits.preference_value: window seat
habits.scope_condition: Flights Kara books for herself for seminars, clinic visits, conferences, or solo positioning legs when she is not coordinating adjacent seats with someone else.

habits.boundary_condition: Treat as a soft default; if true afternoon return departures are unavailable, limited, or unattractive, consider options close to afternoon.
habits.condition: When booking or comparing round-trip flights and selecting the return-leg departure time.
habits.default_action: Search for return-flight options departing in the afternoon and present those first when available.
habits.exception_condition: Do not apply as a universal outbound-leg rule; one supporting dialogue separately used a morning outbound while still preferring an afternoon return.
habits.name: afternoon_return_departure_preference
habits.preference_value: Prefer the return flight to depart in the afternoon.
habits.scope_condition: Round-trip itineraries returning to Tampa after work trips, conferences, or partner weekends when the current trip does not specify a different return window.

habits.boundary_condition: This is a soft customer/review-rating default, not an exact 4-star-only rule, not a hotel-class-star requirement, and not a reusable 4.5-star or 3.5-star threshold by itself.
habits.condition: When searching for hotels and a Google rating, review score, or similar customer-facing rating is available, especially for nice, upscale, resort-style, or high-rated stays.
habits.default_action: Filter or rank toward hotels with customer-facing ratings of at least 4.0 stars and report the rating source when known.
habits.exception_condition: If the user specifies a different threshold, prioritizes a budget stay with an explicit lower floor such as 3.5 stars, asks for the cheapest option regardless of quality, only suitable options fall below 4.0, or the rating metric is unclear, follow or clarify the current trip-specific instruction instead of hard-enforcing the 4.0 default.
habits.name: hotel_four_star_customer_rating_floor
habits.preference_value: Prefer hotels with clearly good customer-facing ratings, normally at least 4.0 stars, while treating higher ratings such as 4.5 as a bonus and lower stated floors as trip-specific exceptions.
habits.scope_condition: Hotel searches for teaching trips, conferences, clinic visits, and personal stays where customer-facing ratings are available.

habits.boundary_condition: Treat this as a reusable hotel-amenity preference, not a destination, date, price, restaurant/bar, or indoor/outdoor pool preference. Use it as soft unless the current request makes the amenities mandatory.
habits.condition: When selecting or evaluating hotel options.
habits.default_action: Prioritize or verify hotels that offer all three amenities: a pool, a hot tub, and fitness or exercise access; clearly note if one is missing.
habits.exception_condition: If otherwise suitable hotels do not offer all three amenities, present close matches while explicitly noting which of pool, hot tub, or fitness/exercise access is absent.
habits.name: prefer_hotel_pool_hot_tub_fitness
habits.preference_value: Prefer hotels with a pool, hot tub, and fitness or exercise access.
habits.scope_condition: Hotel choices for multi-night work stays after long teaching days and for active leisure weekends where recovery facilities affect the stay.

habits.boundary_condition: Evidence supports queen-size beds as the recurring preference. A king bed may be acceptable when explicitly offered or requested, but the evidence does not establish a reusable preference to upgrade to king whenever possible.
habits.condition: When booking a standard hotel room where a single larger/shared bed is appropriate and no separate-bed setup has been requested.

habits.name: queen_bed_for_single_bed_hotel_rooms
habits.preference_value: Prefer a queen-size bed for hotel rooms intended to have one larger/shared bed.
habits.scope_condition: Standard hotel rooms for Kara alone or with her partner when no separate-bed arrangement, accessibility bedding need, or alternate setup has been requested.

habits.boundary_condition: Do not generalize this to other amenities such as microwave, balcony, bar, fireplace, room size, location, dates, or price.
habits.condition: When selecting or comparing hotel rooms and in-room amenities are being considered.
habits.default_action: Use an in-room coffee maker and refrigerator or mini-fridge as soft amenity criteria, and confirm availability when relevant.
habits.exception_condition: If a hotel otherwise strongly matches the current trip, treat a missing coffee maker or refrigerator/mini-fridge as a point to confirm with the user rather than an automatic rejection.
habits.name: hotel_room_coffee_maker_and_fridge_preference
habits.preference_value: Prefers a hotel room with both a coffee maker and a refrigerator or mini-fridge.
habits.scope_condition: Hotel room comparisons for seminar, clinic-training, and conference stays where she needs an easy morning routine and simple food or drink storage.

longitudinal_plan.travel_tempo: Moderately frequent: roughly 9 to 11 work-related trips per year, 2 larger conferences, and 2 to 4 personal or partner trips, with heavier planning in spring and fall seminar seasons.
longitudinal_plan.typical_episode_shape: Most travel episodes span 2 to 4 sessions: initial dates and constraints, flight and hotel shortlist, trade-off refinement, then booking or pre-trip verification. Longer conference or partner-weekend episodes may add sessions for hotel block comparisons, room amenity checks, or return-flight adjustments.

persona.decision_posture: Comfort-practical rather than luxury-first. She cares about reliable hotels, room routines, and physical recovery after long teaching days, while accepting trade-offs when class schedules, conference blocks, or airfare availability dominate.
persona.name: Kara Bennett
persona.occupation: continuing-education instructor for pediatric physical therapists
persona.travel_identity: Self-booking domestic traveler who plans seminar weekends, clinic-training visits, professional conferences, and a few active recovery trips with her partner each year.

travel_contexts.description: Recurring Friday-to-Monday or Saturday-to-Monday trips to teach continuing-education courses at hospitals, therapy practices, and university facilities.
travel_contexts.planning_pattern: Compares flights first around teaching times, then narrows hotels near the host site with attention to room amenities and recovery facilities.

travel_contexts.description: Short solo work trips for on-site demonstrations, staff training, and follow-up coaching.
travel_contexts.planning_pattern: Often needs efficient return travel and dependable hotel basics because mornings start early.

travel_contexts.description: A few larger annual conferences where she may use conference hotels but still checks ratings and room setup before committing.
travel_contexts.planning_pattern: Balances official room blocks against her usual comfort criteria.

travel_contexts.description: Occasional hiking, beach, spa, or race-support weekends with her partner.
travel_contexts.planning_pattern: More willing to spend time comparing hotel amenities, but still treats preferences as soft unless the trip itself makes them central.

communication_style.decision_cues: Responds well to recommendations framed as 'best fit,' 'acceptable backup,' and 'ask before booking' rather than long narrative explanations.
communication_style.follow_up_behavior: Often refines one variable at a time after an initial search, such as moving the departure later, checking a room amenity, or comparing a different airport.
communication_style.planning_preferences: Likes shortlists with the trade-offs called out plainly, especially where timing, connection quality, hotel rating, and room amenities differ.

habit_interactions: For flights, the connection policy and explicit client timing usually matter more than the soft United preference; a non-United itinerary can win when it has a cleaner schedule or better connection.
The afternoon-departure habit fits his Bay Area work rhythm, but it should not be treated as an automatic return-flight rule or as stronger than a fixed meeting time.
The window-seat habit is most visible on solo work flights and becomes less important when he is traveling with his spouse or needs a different seating arrangement.
For hotels, the customer-rating threshold is the main quality screen; restaurant access and the coffee-maker/fridge bundle are practical tie-breakers for suburban work stays.
Personal weekend trips may still show the flight and hotel-quality defaults, but the work-specific room-routine and suburban-dining concerns should be lighter.

habits.boundary_condition: Applies only as a non-exclusive airline preference; United is favored only among otherwise suitable options and may coexist with other acceptable preferred carriers.
habits.condition: When searching for commercial flights and no stronger current-trip carrier instruction overrides this preference.
habits.default_action: Give United positive ranking weight and include United among preferred carrier options when otherwise comparable, while still considering other suitable airlines.
habits.exception_condition: If United is unavailable, worse on primary itinerary constraints such as nonstop/timing/class, materially less attractive, or the user explicitly requests another carrier for the current trip, use or present the better alternative.
habits.name: soft_united_preferred_carrier
habits.preference_value: United is a soft preferred/acceptable airline, not an exclusive carrier requirement.
habits.scope_condition: Applies to Jonah's self-booked commercial flights from Bay Area airports for client visits, distributor meetings, conferences, and comparable personal trips.

habits.exception_condition: If acceptable afternoon departures are unavailable or conflict with other stated constraints, ask before broadening to nearby time windows.

habits.preference_value: Prefers flight departures in the afternoon when no different departure-time constraint is specified.
habits.scope_condition: Applies when Jonah is choosing flight departure times without a stronger meeting-driven or same-day urgency constraint.

longitudinal_plan.travel_tempo: High but uneven over roughly twenty months: several spring and fall client-site bursts, quieter holiday periods, a few annual conferences, and occasional personal weekends.
longitudinal_plan.typical_episode_shape: Most travel episodes span 2 to 4 sessions: initial flight-and-hotel search, one refinement around meeting times or airport choice, booking confirmation, and occasional follow-up for seat choice, room amenities, or hotel comparison. A minority of urgent site visits compress into a single session, while conference trips may generate longer planning threads.

persona.decision_posture: Schedule-reliability focused and practical. He likes comfortable, predictable flights and hotels that support early workdays, but he treats most preferences as soft when a client schedule, route availability, or budget ceiling is more important.
